It is valid if for all reals $a < b$ the pair $(c, d) = \sigma(a, b)$ satisfies $a \le c < d \le b$, so that it answers each nonempty open interval with a nonempty open subinterval, possibly the interval itself. nodes.summary: For every set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, player A has a winning strategy in the Banach–Mazur game for $E$ if and only if there are reals $a < b$ such that $(a, b) \setminus E$ is meagre, and player B has a winning strategy in the Banach–Mazur game for $E$ if and only if $E$ is meagre.
